prompt: Who are the members of the channel that has the message about circuit-tracer hitting OOM errors on large model loads, given that a workspace admin reacted to that message with the eyes emoji?
binding_note: The route requires: conversation membership → conversation (the channel) → message (the OOM/circuit-tracer message) → reaction (eyes emoji) → user (the reactor) → workspace membership (must be owner/admin). The only eyes reaction on that message belongs to a plain member, so no channel qualifies and no membership pair can be returned.

obligations.name: qualifying_channel_membership_report
obligations.description: Select conversation membership pairs (channel_id, user_id) for whichever channel contains a message about circuit-tracer OOM errors that a user holding an owner/admin workspace role reacted to with the eyes emoji; report those membership pairs.
obligations.scope: membership listing for a channel identified via a message-reaction-role chain

task_spec.text: Find the channel holding the circuit-tracer OOM-error message that a workspace admin reacted to with the eyes emoji, then list that channel's members.

access_plan: Use conversations.history/search.messages on #engineering to locate the circuit-tracer OOM message, then reactions.get on that message's timestamp/channel to inspect its reactions and reactor IDs. Cross-check each reactor's workspace role via users.info (owner/admin vs member) rather than the conversation membership role, which channel_members does not store. Only if a reactor qualifies as owner/admin would conversations.members on that channel be used to enumerate membership pairs; here the check fails for the only eyes reactor, so no membership pairs are returned.
